Alice — thanks for the docs and for proposing the window. Wed 6/12 13:00 PT works for Redwood. Owners below — I'll act as exec sponsor during the window.

Planned roles (Redwood):
- Test orchestration / traffic profile: Ben Carter
- Runbook runner / cutover coordinator: Marissa Cole
- Rollback lead / variant switch authority: Karthik Iyer
- Exec sponsor / stakeholder comms: Vivek Kulkarni

Acceptance criteria we will validate during the dry-run:
1) 90th percentile latency meets the agreed SLOs under the ramp profile
2) KV cache warm/repopulate completes within 30s without increased token cost
3) Fallback model variant returns acceptable quality (EVAL > 0.92 on agreed prompt set)
4) Successful region failover with requests routed to fallback capacity within 120s

Ben — please prepare the traffic profiles (synthetic and anonymized real traces). Marissa — can you publish the cutover checklist PDF into the Drive folder and send the link back to Alice and Tim before EOD tomorrow?

Also: propose we run a short chaos pass during the second hour (14:00-14:30) to validate the rollback path. If any of the acceptance checks fail, we will execute the rollback plan and reconvene to triage.

Thanks — Vivek

Quick dry-run update (notes from the session):

Summary:
- Traffic ramp executed (0 -> target QPS over 20 minutes) using synthetic traces and scrubbed samples.
- 95% of endpoints stayed within SLOs. Observed a KV cache warm/repopulate delay on one worker pool (approx 47s).
- Chaos pass (14:05-14:25) induced a region-level latency spike. Fallback variant switch occurred, but routing lagged ~150s on a single shard — still within our rollback-window but larger than target.
